correctness.rationale: The exact three-distance decomposition retains the nonsmooth vertex distance; a strict local positive quadratic remainder plus the wedge geometry bounds the entire rare sublevel by u=O(sqrt(t)), v=O(t^(3/4)). The moving minimum converges to m_lambda; the rescaled cost converges almost everywhere to G_lambda; zero boundary measure and common compact support yield area and L1 density convergence. The t^(5/4) Jacobian, beta/uniform marks, exact relative-excess profile and large-parameter integral limits are reconstructed and checked. The standalone checker numerically compares exact-cost cross-section areas with the asymptotic coefficient for five lambda values/two t thresholds; quadrature is corroboration only.

value.rationale: The 120-degree Fermat–Torricelli change from a vertex minimizer to an interior minimizer is an intrinsic geometric phase transition. The nontrivial anisotropic t^(5/4) crossover provides a precise universal transition profile and conditional near-optimal location geometry, including a natural Beta/uniform decomposition. This is motivated by near-optimal three-focus facility locations and polyellipse area, not a routine restatement of classical minimizer location or an unmotivated finite calculation.
